headline: The National University of Singapore has launched a national centre that will use AI to design microbes and enzymes for making chemicals more sustainably.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: an official national centre launch with named funding, but the release lists aims, not results.
importance_line: Researchers and students in Singapore gain a shared AI and automated-laboratory facility with more than 150 people, and industry may later get cleaner ways to make specialty chemicals, but the centre has only just opened and the release reports goals, not results.
summary: The National University of Singapore (NUS) says it has officially launched the National Centre for Engineering Biology, a national research centre it hosts with five partner institutions, funded by a National Research Foundation grant of close to S$50 million over seven years from 2023, to use AI to design microbes and enzymes (proteins that speed up chemical reactions) that make specialty chemicals from renewable materials. In its new facility, AI models propose designs that an automated laboratory builds and tests in large numbers, starting with functional fatty acids, a type of specialty chemical, and the launch opens Singapore Engineering Biology Week from 5 to 8 October.
notes: Read in full. NUS's own news release. The S$50 million is the National Research Foundation grant awarded in 2023, not new money; the launch itself (5 Oct 2026, tied to the opening of Engineering Biology Week) is the news. No results are reported.
